ocr_errors.image: Do. LAudasse arguor indignum. Ra. Malum quidem quod est
ocr_errors.ocr: *Do.* Laudasſe arguor indignum. … *Ra.* Laudasſe arguor indignum. Malum quidem
ocr_errors.effect_on_english: spurious sentence in Reason's reply: 'You are accused of having praised someone unworthy.'

causes.finding: 'to be deceived is foreign to one's nature' for 'Falli enim alienum' (another's doing)
causes.image: Falli enim alienum ; fallere autem, proprium fallentis est crimen
causes.ocr: Falli enim alienum; fallere autem, proprium fallentis eſt crimen
causes.english: For to be deceived is foreign to one's nature

causes.finding: 'even more prone to praise' drops 'aequo' (than is just)
causes.image: Hinc ad laudandum, æquo etiam proniores sunt
causes.ocr: Hinc ad laudandum, æquo etiam proniores ſunt
causes.english: Hence, they are even more prone to praise

causes.finding: 'You alone cherish me' turns imperative 'Tu me sola ... refove' into a statement
causes.image: Tu me solâ sinu pio refove, sic non famæ tantum
causes.ocr: Tu me ſolâ ſinu pio refove, ſic non famæ tantum
causes.english: You alone cherish me with a pious bosom

causes.finding: (not flagged by judges) Reason's reply opens with a sentence not on the page
causes.image: Ra. Malum quidem quod est, bonâ sæpe oritur radice
causes.ocr: *Ra.* Laudasſe arguor indignum. Malum quidem quod eſt
causes.english: You are accused of having praised someone unworthy.

note: Clean 1649 print; OCR is right except that it repeats 'Laudasse arguor indignum' after 'Ra.' (the drop-initial L line belongs only to Do.), which the English renders as an extra sentence. All three judge findings are minor and sit where OCR = image.
